title: Everything in IT Ops
sub: What IT Ops does from the first alert to a verified fix, and what keeps it under your control.

items: Merges duplicate alerts from many tools into one incident
Service, environment and owner taken from your service catalog
Covers service outages, resource exhaustion and bad deployments
Optional monitoring of metrics, logs, traces, deployments and databases
Monitoring agents for Linux, Windows and Kubernetes, no code changes
Service map, service level objectives (SLOs) and charts on each incident
Finds the root cause and ties every claim to evidence
Flags unsupported claims and names data sources it could not reach
The AI investigator has read-only access to your systems
Recalls past incidents and only the fixes confirmed to work
Instructions hidden in logs or alerts are treated as data, never obeyed
Team ratings of each investigation guide when to expand automation
Fixes come only from an approved catalog, never free-form commands
Linux: service restart, process stop, log and temp file cleanup
Windows and IIS: service restart, process stop, app pool recycle, cleanup
Kubernetes: change report, pod and rollout restarts, rollout undo, scale-up
Argo CD and Helm rollback to a previous release; Docker container restart
PostgreSQL and MySQL: connection pool check, stop long-running queries
Disk, port, health, DNS, connectivity and certificate expiry checks
Risk levels from look-only to forbidden; policy can only raise them
Caps on targets per action; systems not on your list are refused
Approval required during change freeze windows
Four-eyes rule: nobody can approve their own request
Approval cards show evidence, dry-run result and rollback plan
Approvals expire and are void if target or parameters change
Staged rollout: observe, suggest, act in test, then in production
Dry run before every change
Success measured by metrics and health checks, not the AI's opinion
Automatic rollback and handover to a person if checks fail
Temporary changes revert on their own when their time runs out
One emergency stop halts every automated change, even rollback
Append-only, tamper-evident audit log of every step
Any later edit is caught against an external copy of the log
Audit records flow to your security monitoring system (SIEM)
Value report on screen and as PDF: incidents, actions, rollbacks
Your name and logo on tickets, chat cards and PDFs
Monitoring: Prometheus Alertmanager, Grafana, Zabbix and Datadog
Logs and cloud: Splunk, Azure Monitor and AWS CloudWatch
Webhook, email or API intake for SolarWinds, PRTG, Nagios and more
Tickets in Jira or ServiceNow; approvals in Microsoft Teams or Slack
AI provider: Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock or OpenAI-compatible
Documented REST API with OpenAPI, plus CSV and NDJSON export
Sign-in via Entra ID, Okta, AD FS, Active Directory or OpenLDAP
Viewer, operator and admin roles; unmapped users cannot sign in
Local emergency admin account if your identity provider is down
One Linux server with Docker Compose, or Kubernetes with Helm
Air-gapped install from one offline bundle with a local AI model
Secrets and personal data masked before any text reaches the AI

specs.v: In your environment: one Linux server, Kubernetes, private cloud or fully air-gapped
Linux, Windows and IIS, Kubernetes, Docker, Argo CD, Helm, PostgreSQL and MySQL
Zabbix, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Splunk, CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Jira, ServiceNow, Teams, Slack
SSO via OIDC or SAML 2.0, AD and LDAP; viewer, operator and admin roles
Single-tenant; sensitive text masked before the AI; KVKK (Türkiye's data protection law) erasure requests honored
Interface and documentation in Turkish and English

gaps: Core safety rules are built into the product, not settings: no configuration, license or AI output can relax them. A strong CISO argument the page lacks.
Emergency stop, read access and rejecting approvals keep working even after the license expires, which answers a lock-in worry.
The deck promises no numbers: gains are measured with the customer on their own incidents during the pilot, and savings use only figures they enter.
KVKK, Türkiye's data protection law: personal data erasure requests are honored, even in the audit log. The page never mentions it.
The deck asks whether an instruction hidden in a log line can steer automation. The page never answers this prompt injection worry.
A CISO architecture document, data flow and security questionnaire answers are offered on request; the page does not say so.
